history.dynasty: Later Chera (10th-c. inscriptions of Goda Ravi Varma); Kingdom of Tanur (Vettathunad), vassals of the Zamorin of Calicut
history.period: 10th century CE onwards; inscriptions of the Later Chera ruler Goda Ravi Varma
history.summary: Ancient two-storied shrine (gaja-prishta kovil — shaped like an elephant's back) at Triprangode village, noted in the 15th-century Kokila Sandesa as a major destination of northern Kerala. Legend says Shiva killed Yama here in seven steps to save the boy Markandeya, with a pratishta at each step — the moolasthanam 'Karanayil' plus three further Shiva shrines. Inscriptions of Later Chera ruler Goda Ravi Varma (10th c.) were found here; later the area was in Vettathunad (Tanur), and the Zamorin's army camped at Triprangode during the Thirunavaya Wars of the 14th century. The famous offering is Sayanapradakshinam (rolling circumambulation). Managed by the Malabar Devaswom Board. CSV town/state (Malappuram, Kerala) are correct; the town is Triprangode, near Tirur.

name: Triprangode Siva Temple
town_description: Triprangode is a temple village near Tirur in the Malappuram coast belt, spread over ~6 acres of temple grounds with ponds and sub-shrines, known across northern Kerala for its Markandeya legend.
